title: Gyoza
subtitle: Japanese pan-fried pork and cabbage dumplings
excerpt: The Japanese dumpling: thin-skinned parcels filled with pork mince, cabbage, garlic, and ginger, pleated at the top and cooked in the classic yaki-gyoza style: fried until crisp on the base, then steamed in the same pan until the filling is cooked through.

recipe.sourceNotes: Gyoza are the Japanese version of the Chinese jiaozi, brought to Japan by soldiers and migrants returning from China after the Second World War and rapidly adapted into a form that is now distinctly Japanese. Yaki-gyoza (pan-fried) is the most common preparation in Japan, characterised by the two-stage cooking method: a brief fry in hot oil to set the base, then steam with water (sometimes with a slurry of flour and water to create a lacy skirt), then a final crisping. The thin wrapper is one of the key differences from Chinese dumplings, which use a thicker dough. Gyoza wrappers are widely available in Asian supermarkets; making them from scratch is excellent but significantly more time-consuming.

recipeTools.notes: A non-stick frying pan with a lid.

content.text: Squeeze the cabbage very dry after salting: excess water makes the filling wet and prevents the base from crisping. Pleat the wrappers firmly so they seal completely; any gap will cause them to burst open during cooking. The steam stage is done with a lid on; remove the lid for the final 1 to 2 minutes to re-crisp the base. Work in batches if your pan cannot hold all the gyoza flat without overlapping.

items.preparation: very finely shredded; tossed with 0.5 tsp salt, left for 10 minutes, then squeezed very dry
for wrappers; or use 30 ready-made gyoza wrappers

content.text: Make the wrappers (or use shop-bought): mix the flour with 100 ml of just-boiled water and knead into a smooth dough. Rest for 20 minutes. Roll into a log, cut into 30 pieces, and roll each into a thin 8 cm circle.

Mix the filling: combine the pork, squeezed cabbage, garlic, ginger, spring onion, soy sauce, and sesame oil. Stir vigorously in one direction until the mixture is sticky and cohesive. Place a teaspoon of filling in the centre of each wrapper, dampen the edge with water, fold into a half-moon, and pleat the edge firmly to seal.

Heat the oil in a non-stick frying pan over medium-high heat. Add the gyoza flat-side down and fry for 2 minutes until golden on the base. Pour in 80 ml of water, cover immediately, and steam for 5 to 6 minutes until the water has evaporated. Remove the lid and cook for 1 more minute to re-crisp the base. Serve with the dipping sauce.
